title: Flat base change of blow-ups
statement:
The constructed comparison $\operatorname{bc}_g$ is an isomorphism over
$Y$.

proof.text: Use the data of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]: $g:Y\to X$ is flat, $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent, $\mathcal J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$, $B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(Y)$, and $T=Y\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$. Write $f=\operatorname{bc}_g:B\to T$. By [lemma-nagata-flat-pullback-rees], the canonical map $\beta_g:g^*\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I)\to\mathcal R_Y(\mathcal J)$ is a graded algebra equivalence. Its degree-zero map is the canonical identification $g^*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_Y$: this is the $n=0$ component of the canonical maps in [def-nagata-flat-pullback-rees-map]. Thus it preserves the chosen degree-zero structural maps, as required when applying relative Proj.

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up, proof; compare the current blueprint proof of thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change

proof.text: Let $a:B\xrightarrow{\sim}P_Y(\mathcal R_Y(\mathcal J))$ and $d:Y\times_X P_X(\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I))\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ denote the chart-preserving identifications in [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. For each affine open $W\subseteq Y$, the restriction of the specified comparison is exactly $f_W=d_W\circ(c_g)_W\circ P_Y(\beta_g)_W\circ a_W$, by the displayed composite in that definition. Apply clause (2) of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] to the graded equivalence from Step 1: contravariance gives an isomorphism from the Proj of $\mathcal R_Y(\mathcal J)$ to the Proj of $g^*\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I)$. Clause (4), with the given flat $g$, gives the isomorphism $c_g$ to $Y\times_X P_X(\mathcal R_X(\mathcal I))$. Clause (1) identifies the affine-base restrictions. All four factors are over $W$: the middle maps respect the degree-zero structural maps and the coefficientwise base-change structure, and the outer identifications respect the chosen local models and structure morphisms, as specified in the comparison definition. Thus $f_W$ is an isomorphism over $W$; its inverse is $a_W^{-1}\circ P_Y(\beta_g)_W^{-1}\circ(c_g)_W^{-1}\circ d_W^{-1}$, with the inverse equations obtained by cancelling adjacent inverse factors. Here restriction means inverse image of $W$ under each structure map to $Y$, and makes no claim that a blow-up is affine.

proof.text: Choose the affine open cover $(W_a)$ of $Y$ used to construct $f$ and write $h_a=(f_{W_a})^{-1}:T|_{W_a}\to B|_{W_a}$. These inverse maps are over $W_a$. On $W_a\cap W_b$ both $f_{W_a}$ and $f_{W_b}$ restrict to the same map $f_{ab}$, since they are restrictions of the specified global $f$. Their inverses restrict to inverses of $f_{ab}$, so they agree: if $u$ and $v$ are these inverses, then $u=u\circ(f_{ab}\circ v)=(u\circ f_{ab})\circ v=v$. Regard $h_a$ as a map $T|_{W_a}\to B$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to obtain $h:T\to B$. The opens $T|_{W_a}$ cover $T$, and $B|_{W_a}$ cover $B$. On these covers $f\circ h$ and $h\circ f$ are respectively the identities, by the local inverse equations. The uniqueness assertion of the same gluing node gives $f\circ h=1_T$ and $h\circ f=1_B$. This proves that the constructed comparison itself is an isomorphism; it does not merely produce an unspecified isomorphism between the two schemes.

source.place: Tag 01JA, section-glueing-schemes, mapping property in lemma-glue; inverse-gluing argument for Tag 0805 expanded

proof.text: Let $p:B\to Y$ and $q:T\to Y$ be the structure maps. Step 2 gives $q\circ f=p$ locally on the cover of $B$, hence globally by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Composing with the inverse $h$ of Step 3 gives $p\circ h=q\circ f\circ h=q$. Thus $f$ and its inverse are morphisms over $Y$, proving the asserted isomorphism over $Y$.
